title: Institute of Law, Policy Research and Human Rights Limited v The Attorney General (Brian Mundubile, Interested Party) [2024] ZMCC 25 (13 November 2024)
case_name: Institute of Law, Policy Research and Human Rights Limited v The Attorney General
issue_tags: Article 74(2) — appointment/election of the Leader of the Opposition
Originating Summons — Order IV rule 2(2) Constitutional Court Rules
Article 2 — duty to defend the Constitution
Speaker of the National Assembly — 1 November 2023 replacement of Leader of the Opposition
outcome_detail: Originating Summons (Order IV rule 2(2) Constitutional Court Rules) by the Institute of Law, Policy Research and Human Rights Limited seeking interpretation of Article 74(2) of the Constitution on the appointment and election of the Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly dismissed (paragraph [57]: "It follows that we are of the firm view that this is not a suitable case for interpretation of the stated provisions. It is dismissed"). The 11-judge Court held that the questions were not prospective (the underlying events — the Speaker's 1 November 2023 replacement of the Leader of the Opposition — had already taken place and were fiercely contested with parallel litigation), and the questions were personalised rather than generalised, requiring a proper trial rather than abstract constitutional interpretation. Originating Summons not the right mode of commencement. Each party bears their own costs (paragraph [60]).
